scope: Integrate the certified Command Center production GLB into the existing React Three Fiber Command Center runtime without changing movement, topology, camera, interaction, Ask, HUD, route, or fallback authority.
Use the existing BLENDER_ART_ASSETS and BLENDER_ART_PLACEMENTS registry as the asset path and placement authority.
Replace only procedural decorative Command Center scenery that would visually duplicate the certified GLB.
Keep InteractionStation rendering, movement target marker, runtime lighting/fog required by the scene, and all React-owned behavior intact.
Add a bounded Suspense/error fallback for Command Center decorative scenery so an asset loading failure does not destroy world navigation or conventional routes.
Add or update focused tests/evidence proving the GLB integration boundary.
Do not merge, deploy, or modify other districts in this task.
acceptance: Task executes from exact certified export candidate SHA 890f584306b6a44c4bf5d325591cb7e9ee1bf718.
public/world/art/command-center.glb remains byte-for-byte unchanged with SHA-256 72008b693cf0fc889aea7cf8af94ec2876cc0e3a7807b430e6e483fe275d7496 and size 845512 bytes.
The runtime loads the Command Center GLB through BLENDER_ART_ASSETS['command-center'] and BLENDER_ART_PLACEMENTS['command-center'] rather than introducing duplicate asset path or placement literals.
The GLB is decorative scenery only; no topology, walkability, station, content, spawn, bridge, camera, Ask, or navigation authority is inferred from GLB meshes or object names.
Ask Terminal remains React-owned and uses the existing station configuration and interaction behavior.
Player spawn, movement, click/tap/keyboard controls, camera rig, bridges, world bounds, and zone topology remain unchanged.
Current procedural decorative geometry that would duplicate the certified GLB is removed or replaced without removing interaction stations, movement target feedback, or required runtime lights/fog.
Command Center asset loading is bounded by Suspense and a local decorative failure fallback so an asset failure does not take down navigation or conventional routes.
Other districts and their lazy-loading behavior remain unchanged.
Conventional routes and no-WebGL fallback remain unchanged.
Focused tests/evidence document the integration boundary and protect the asset registry/runtime ownership rules.
Independent Terra review returns pass with no required fixes.
No merge to main and no deployment occurs.
stop_conditions: The certified export candidate ref no longer resolves to 890f584306b6a44c4bf5d325591cb7e9ee1bf718.
The production GLB hash or byte size changes.
Integration requires changing world topology, spawn, bridges, camera, interaction station coordinates/content, Ask behavior, WorldEntry, PlayerController, or deployment configuration.
A proposed implementation derives gameplay or content authority from GLB meshes/object names.
Asset failure handling would require removing existing conventional/WebGL fallback behavior.
Automated repository verification fails and cannot be repaired inside the declared runtime/test write scope.
Independent review returns fix_required or stop.
